items.stem: Define the term 'analysis (systems life cycle)'.
items.answer: The stage in which the current system is studied, using research methods, to identify its problems and the requirements of the new system.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: The stage in which the current system is studied, using research methods, to identify its problems and the requirements of the new system. [2]

items.stem: Explain why the analysis stage is important.
items.answer: It identifies the problems with the current system and the exact requirements of users, so the new system is designed to solve the right problems; mistakes here are costly to fix later.
items.markingKey: 1 mark identifies problems/requirements; 1 mark consequence of poor analysis. [2]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of interviews compared with questionnaires.
items.answer: Advantage: detailed answers and follow-up questions. Disadvantage: time-consuming and expensive, so only a few people can be interviewed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark advantage; 1 mark disadvantage. [2]

items.stem: Leila, a systems analyst, is investigating the stock control system at Vista Estate Agents in Singapore. Describe what the analyst would look for in the current documents.
items.answer: Data items recorded; formats; volumes; outputs produced; duplication.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per point, max 2. [2]

items.stem: Ana, a systems analyst, is investigating the stock control system at Horizon Travel in Toronto. (a) Explain the difference between user requirements and system requirements. (b) Describe what the analyst would look for in the current documents.
items.answer: (a) User: what users need in their terms; system: hardware/software/functions to meet them. (b) Data items recorded; formats; volumes; outputs produced; duplication.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each. [2] (b) 1 mark per point, max 2. [2]

items.stem: Lakeside College, a college in Seoul, has asked a systems analyst to replace its paper-based booking system. Discuss which research method the analyst at Lakeside College should rely on most.
items.answer: Points for: interviews give detail; questionnaires reach many; observation shows reality; documents show data. Points against / limitations: each method has weaknesses; relying on one gives an incomplete picture; time and cost limits. Conclusion: a combination of methods is best, chosen to suit the size and type of organisation.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks points developed and applied with a conclusion. Indicative content — for: interviews give detail; questionnaires reach many; observation shows reality; documents show data. Against: each method has weaknesses; relying on one gives an incomplete picture; time and cost limits. Conclusion may argue: a combination of methods is best, chosen to suit the size and type of organisation. [4]

items.stem: Describe the difference between 'document analysis' and 'user requirements'.
items.answer: document analysis: Examining the documents used in the current system, such as forms, invoices and reports, to find what data is input, processed and output. user requirements: What the users need the new system to do, stated in their own terms.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: document analysis correctly described; 1 mark: user requirements correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between 'system requirements' and 'document analysis'.
items.answer: system requirements: A specification of the hardware, software and functions the new system needs to meet the user requirements. document analysis: Examining the documents used in the current system, such as forms, invoices and reports, to find what data is input, processed and output.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: system requirements correctly described; 1 mark: document analysis correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Which research method is most suitable for finding out which data fields are on the current paper order forms and invoices?
items.answer: Document analysis
items.markingKey: document analysis: shows exactly what data is recorded and output; reveals volumes and formats.

items.stem: An analyst at Orbit Games Studio in Nairobi needs to do the following: finding out which data fields are on the current paper order forms and invoices. Recommend a research method, and give one advantage and one disadvantage of it.
items.answer: Document analysis. Advantage: shows exactly what data is recorded and output; reveals volumes and formats. Disadvantage: documents may be out of date; does not show problems or how staff really work.
items.markingKey: 1 mark method (document analysis); 1 mark advantage (shows exactly what data is recorded and output; reveals volumes and formats); 1 mark disadvantage (documents may be out of date; does not show problems or how staff really work). [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'data flow diagram (DFD)'.
items.answer: A diagram showing how data moves through a system between external entities, processes and data stores.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: A diagram showing how data moves through a system between external entities, processes and data stores. [2]

items.stem: Explain why the designer produces a DFD before writing any code.
items.answer: It shows clearly what data enters, is processed, is stored and leaves the system, so the requirements can be checked with users and the processes and files can be designed correctly.
items.markingKey: 1 mark shows data movement; 1 mark check/plan processes and files. [2]

items.stem: Explain two features of good input screen design.
items.answer: Logical order matching source documents; clear labels and instructions; drop-down lists/validation; consistent layout; error messages; not overcrowded.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark point, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Chloe is designing a new ordering system for BlueWave Supermarkets in Cairo. Explain what an entity-relationship diagram shows.
items.answer: Entities and the type of relationship between them (1:1, 1:M, M:M).
items.markingKey: 1 mark entities; 1 mark relationships. [2]

items.stem: BlueWave Supermarkets in Istanbul has approved the analysis of its new booking system and design is starting. (a) Describe two features of a well-designed output report. (b) Explain why test plans are designed at this stage.
items.answer: (a) Clear title and headings; only relevant data; totals/summaries; sorted; date and page numbers. (b) To check later that the system meets the design and requirements.

items.answer: A diagram showing the overall flow of data through a system, including inputs, processes, files and outputs, using standard symbols.

items.answer: A diagram showing the entities in a system and the relationships (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many) between them.

items.stem: Define the term 'test plan'.
items.answer: A document listing each test to be carried out, with its purpose, the test data, the expected result and space for the actual result.

items.answer: Normal data checks that the system processes valid input correctly; abnormal data checks that invalid input is rejected with a suitable message rather than crashing or being stored.

items.stem: Explain the difference between alpha and beta testing.
items.answer: Alpha testing is done in-house by the developers/testers before release; beta testing is done by real users outside the company on a nearly complete version.
items.markingKey: 1 mark alpha; 1 mark beta. [2]

items.stem: Atlas Museum in Doha is about to release a new stock-control program. Explain the purpose of beta testing.
items.answer: Real users find problems not found in-house before full release.
items.markingKey: 1 mark real users; 1 mark find remaining bugs. [2]

items.stem: MetroBus in Seoul is about to release a new stock-control program. (a) Explain why extreme test data is important. (b) Explain the purpose of beta testing.
items.answer: (a) Errors often occur at boundaries (e.g. < instead of <=). (b) Real users find problems not found in-house before full release.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark boundaries; 1 mark example error. [2] (b) 1 mark real users; 1 mark find remaining bugs. [2]

items.stem: Sunrise Bakery in Auckland is about to release a new stock-control program. Evaluate whether Sunrise Bakery should release the system after alpha testing only.
items.answer: Points for: quicker release; lower cost; developers know the system. Points against / limitations: developers miss real-world use cases; bugs found by customers damage reputation; beta testing gives user feedback. Conclusion: beta testing is usually worthwhile for systems used by many people.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks points developed and applied with a conclusion. Indicative content — for: quicker release; lower cost; developers know the system. Conclusion may argue: beta testing is usually worthwhile for systems used by many people. [4]

items.stem: Explain the difference between 'normal test data' and 'abnormal (erroneous) test data'.
items.answer: normal test data: Valid data that the system should accept and process correctly. abnormal (erroneous) test data: Invalid data that the system should reject, such as a value of the wrong type or outside the allowed range.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: normal test data correctly described; 1 mark: abnormal (erroneous) test data correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Describe the difference between 'beta testing' and 'extreme test data'.

items.markingKey: 1 mark: beta testing correctly described; 1 mark: extreme test data correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Priya is planning how to introduce a new system at Sunrise Bakery in Seoul, which has several branches. Evaluate which implementation method Sunrise Bakery should use for its new system.
items.answer: Points for: parallel is safest; pilot limits risk to one site; phased spreads training; direct is quickest and cheapest. Points against / limitations: parallel is costly; pilot is slow to roll out; phased can cause compatibility issues between old and new parts; direct is risky. Conclusion: the choice depends on how critical the system is, its size and the budget.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks developed points on one or both sides; 5-6 marks balanced, applied discussion with a justified conclusion. Indicative content — for: parallel is safest; pilot limits risk to one site; phased spreads training; direct is quickest and cheapest. Against: parallel is costly; pilot is slow to roll out; phased can cause compatibility issues between old and new parts; direct is risky. Conclusion may argue: the choice depends on how critical the system is, its size and the budget. [6]

items.stem: Explain what is meant by the term 'system requirements'.
items.answer: A specification of the hardware, software and functions the new system needs to meet the user requirements.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: A specification of the hardware, software and functions the new system needs to meet the user requirements. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between 'analysis (systems life cycle)' and 'document analysis'.
items.answer: analysis (systems life cycle): The stage in which the current system is studied, using research methods, to identify its problems and the requirements of the new system. document analysis: Examining the documents used in the current system, such as forms, invoices and reports, to find what data is input, processed and output.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: analysis (systems life cycle) correctly described; 1 mark: document analysis correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Palm Grove Hotel, a hotel in Manila, has asked a systems analyst to replace its paper-based booking system. Explain the difference between user requirements and system requirements.
items.answer: User: what users need in their terms; system: hardware/software/functions to meet them.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each. [2]

items.stem: Horizon Travel, a travel agency in Lagos, has asked a systems analyst to replace its paper-based booking system. Discuss which research method the analyst at Horizon Travel should rely on most.
items.answer: Points for: interviews give detail; questionnaires reach many; observation shows reality; documents show data. Points against / limitations: each method has weaknesses; relying on one gives an incomplete picture; time and cost limits. Conclusion: a combination of methods is best, chosen to suit the size and type of organisation.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks points developed and applied with a conclusion. Indicative content — for: interviews give detail; questionnaires reach many; observation shows reality; documents show data. Against: each method has weaknesses; relying on one gives an incomplete picture; time and cost limits. Conclusion may argue: a combination of methods is best, chosen to suit the size and type of organisation. [4]

items.stem: State what is meant by 'output design'.
items.answer: Planning how information will be presented, such as screen layouts and report formats, to meet user needs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: Planning how information will be presented, such as screen layouts and report formats, to meet user needs. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between 'system flowchart' and 'output design'.
items.answer: system flowchart: A diagram showing the overall flow of data through a system, including inputs, processes, files and outputs, using standard symbols. output design: Planning how information will be presented, such as screen layouts and report formats, to meet user needs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: system flowchart correctly described; 1 mark: output design correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Assertion (A): A link entity resolves a many-to-many relationship. Reason (R): Each original entity has a one-to-many relationship with the link entity. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
items.markingKey: A is true and R explains why A is true.

items.stem: Sunrise Bakery in Santiago has approved the analysis of its new booking system and design is starting. Explain why test plans are designed at this stage.
items.answer: To check later that the system meets the design and requirements.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part. [2]

items.stem: Noah is designing a new ordering system for Sunrise Bakery in Accra. Explain why test plans are designed at this stage.
items.answer: To check later that the system meets the design and requirements.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part. [2]

items.stem: BlueWave Supermarkets in Dhaka has approved the analysis of its new booking system and design is starting. Assess the importance of thorough design documentation for the new system at BlueWave Supermarkets.
items.answer: Points for: guides developers; allows checking with users; supports testing and maintenance. Points against / limitations: takes time and cost; may become outdated if requirements change; can delay development. Conclusion: good design documents save much more time later than they cost, especially for maintenance.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks developed points on one or both sides; 5-6 marks balanced, applied discussion with a justified conclusion. Indicative content — for: guides developers; allows checking with users; supports testing and maintenance. Against: takes time and cost; may become outdated if requirements change; can delay development. Conclusion may argue: good design documents save much more time later than they cost, especially for maintenance. [6]

items.stem: Explain what is meant by the term 'abnormal (erroneous) test data'.
items.answer: Invalid data that the system should reject, such as a value of the wrong type or outside the allowed range.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: Invalid data that the system should reject, such as a value of the wrong type or outside the allowed range. [2]

items.stem: Assertion (A): A test plan includes expected results. Reason (R): Beta testing is done only by the programmers. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: A is true but R is false
items.markingKey: A is true; R is false: "Beta testing is done only by the programmers." is incorrect.

items.stem: Palm Grove Hotel in Madrid has a field "number of tickets" that must be a whole number from 1 to 8. Complete a test plan with 3 tests, giving the test data, the type of test data and the expected result for each.
items.answer: 4 (normal) → accepted; 1 (extreme) → accepted; 9 (abnormal) → rejected with error message
items.markingKey: 1 mark per correct row (data + type + expected result), e.g. 4 (normal) → accepted; 1 (extreme) → accepted; 9 (abnormal) → rejected with error message. [3]

items.stem: Leila is testing a new online booking system for Northfield Academy in Madrid. Evaluate whether Northfield Academy should release the system after alpha testing only.
items.answer: Points for: quicker release; lower cost; developers know the system. Points against / limitations: developers miss real-world use cases; bugs found by customers damage reputation; beta testing gives user feedback. Conclusion: beta testing is usually worthwhile for systems used by many people.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks points developed and applied with a conclusion. Indicative content — for: quicker release; lower cost; developers know the system. Against: developers miss real-world use cases; bugs found by customers damage reputation; beta testing gives user feedback. Conclusion may argue: beta testing is usually worthwhile for systems used by many people. [4]

items.stem: Distinguish between 'user documentation' and 'technical documentation'.
items.answer: user documentation: Documentation that explains how to use the system, such as how to log in, enter data, print reports and deal with error messages. technical documentation: Documentation for people who will maintain or develop the system, such as program listings, data dictionaries, flowcharts and design details.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: user documentation correctly described; 1 mark: technical documentation correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Distinguish between 'technical documentation' and 'phased implementation'.
items.answer: technical documentation: Documentation for people who will maintain or develop the system, such as program listings, data dictionaries, flowcharts and design details. phased implementation: Introducing the new system one module or part at a time until the whole system is in use.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: technical documentation correctly described; 1 mark: phased implementation correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: BlueWave Supermarkets, a supermarket chain in Nairobi, is about to implement a new computerised system. Describe the three types of maintenance.
items.answer: Corrective (fix bugs); adaptive (change for new requirements/environment); perfective (improve performance/features).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each. [3]

items.stem: Which implementation method is most suitable for a hospital replacing its patient-records system, where any failure could put lives at risk?
items.answer: Parallel
items.markingKey: parallel: the old system keeps running, so if the new one fails nothing is lost; results can be compared.

items.stem: Mateo is planning how to introduce a new system at MetroBus in Nairobi, which has several branches. Describe the three types of maintenance.
items.answer: Corrective (fix bugs); adaptive (change for new requirements/environment); perfective (improve performance/features).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each. [3]

items.stem: Northfield Academy, a school in Muscat, is about to implement a new computerised system. (a) Explain how the new system would be evaluated. (b) Describe the three types of maintenance.
items.answer: (a) Compare with requirements; gather user feedback; measure performance; identify limitations and improvements. (b) Corrective (fix bugs); adaptive (change for new requirements/environment); perfective (improve performance/features).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per point, max 3. [3] (b) 1 mark each. [3]
